title: Expired, untrusted, incomplete
summary: The three failures you'll see most, what each error message means, and how to tell them apart.

steps.title: Three ways a chain fails
body: When validation fails, ask three questions in this order:
| Question | If not... | .NET `X509ChainStatusFlags` | Chrome says |
| Can I build a path to *some* root? | **incomplete chain**: an intermediate is missing | `PartialChain` | `NET::ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID` |
| Is that root in my trust store? | **untrusted root** (self-signed, private CA, MITM proxy) | `UntrustedRoot` | `NET::ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID` |
| Is every certificate within its dates *right now*? | **expired / not yet valid** | `NotTimeValid` | `NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID` |
Note that "now" is the **client's** clock. A laptop with a dead CMOS battery that thinks it's 2001 rejects every certificate on earth.
In .NET client code all of these surface as `SslPolicyErrors.RemoteCertificateChainErrors` and an
`AuthenticationException: The remote certificate is invalid according to the validation procedure`. The details are in the chain status.

steps.prompt: Match each error to its most likely cause.
pairs: its certificate expired at the weekend
a self-signed dev certificate that isn't trusted
the server doesn't send its intermediate
a TLS-inspecting proxy re-signs traffic with the company's own root

prompt: Every HTTPS site fails on one kiosk PC with `NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID`. The certificates are fine on every other machine. What do you check first?
steps.explain: *Every* site failing, with a *date* error, on *one* machine: the common factor is that machine's clock.

steps.title: An expired intermediate counts too
body: Dates are checked on **every** certificate in the chain, not only the leaf. A freshly renewed leaf still fails if the server sends an
**old, expired intermediate** alongside it.
```text
leaf           Not After: 2031-03-01     ok
intermediate   Not After: 2030-12-31     EXPIRED  -> whole chain NotTimeValid
root           Not After: 2045-01-01     ok
Real-world example: when an old root that many chains led to expired in 2021, servers still sending a cross-signed
intermediate pointing to that root broke older clients. The fix is always the same: serve the chain the CA currently hands out.
Check on the command line:
```text
openssl s_client -connect shop.example:443 -showcerts      shows exactly what the server sends
openssl x509 -in cert.pem -noout -dates                    prints notBefore / notAfter

steps.prompt: A teammate renewed the leaf certificate yesterday, but clients still report `NotTimeValid`. `openssl s_client -showcerts` shows the leaf is fine. What is the next most likely cause?
options: The server is still sending an expired intermediate in its chain file
steps.explain: Every certificate in the chain must be in date. Replace the chain file too, not just the leaf.

steps.prompt: `DojoStatuses(...)` builds a chain trusting `root`, with `sent` as the extra certificates, checked at 1 June of `year`, and returns the status flags; `Show` joins them with commas or prints `(ok)`. The leaf `shortLived` is valid 2030 to 2031. What does it print?
code: var inter = DojoCert("CN=Issuing CA", root, true);
var shortLived = DojoCert("CN=short.example", inter, false, null, null, 2030, 2031);
string Show(X509ChainStatusFlags[] f) => f.Length == 0 ? "(ok)" : string.Join(",", f);
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);
X509ChainStatusFlags[] DojoStatuses(X509Certificate2 leaf, X509Certificate2? trustedRoot, List<X509Certificate2> sent, int year, string? eku = null)
steps.explain: Valid; missing intermediate; complete chain but the root isn't trusted (the server even sent it, which doesn't help); and the leaf expired before mid-2032.

steps.prompt: Is this a **trust** problem or a **time** problem?
items: a self-signed certificate from a colleague
the client's clock is set to 2019

steps.title: Diagnose a status list
prompt: Support tickets paste the chain status. Write `string Diagnose(X509ChainStatusFlags[] statuses)` that returns one verdict,
5. anything else -> `"other: "` followed by the flags joined with `,`
**Run checks** feeds it statuses from real chains as well as hand-made lists.
solution: if (statuses.Contains(X509ChainStatusFlags.NotTimeValid)) return "expired or not yet valid";
hints: Check in the stated order and return as soon as one matches.
template: var dojoInter = DojoCert("CN=Issuing CA", dojoRoot, true);
Dojo.Eq("valid chain", "ok", Diagnose(DojoStatuses(dojoLeaf, dojoRoot, new() { dojoInter }, 2031)));
Dojo.Eq("intermediate not sent", "missing intermediate", Diagnose(DojoStatuses(dojoLeaf, dojoRoot, new(), 2031)));
Dojo.Eq("root not trusted", "untrusted root", Diagnose(DojoStatuses(dojoLeaf, null, new() { dojoInter, dojoRoot }, 2031)));
Dojo.Eq("checked in 2036, after everything expired", "expired or not yet valid", Diagnose(DojoStatuses(dojoLeaf, dojoRoot, new() { dojoInter }, 2036)));
Dojo.Eq("untrusted beats expired", "untrusted root", Diagnose(new[] { X509ChainStatusFlags.NotTimeValid, X509ChainStatusFlags.UntrustedRoot }));
Dojo.Eq("other flags", "other: Revoked,NotValidForUsage", Diagnose(new[] { X509ChainStatusFlags.Revoked, X509ChainStatusFlags.NotValidForUsage }));
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);
X509ChainStatusFlags[] DojoStatuses(X509Certificate2 leaf, X509Certificate2? trustedRoot, List<X509Certificate2> sent, int year, string? eku = null)
